title: LoDA-SA K1=128 full production vs FlashAttention2 decode attention-speedup
method: LoDA-SA K1=128 + tail32 subspace + cmp_ratio=4 + sink4 + swa128 + page64

protocol.prompt: deterministic synthetic paged KV cache, no model weights
protocol.timing: cuda Event per-step, warmup 20 + reps 100, median
protocol.gpus: 8× H20-3e: pc33 GPU0/1, pc40 GPU0/1, pc02 GPU1/2/3, pc31 GPU1

key_findings: TLI attn latency is nearly CONSTANT across context length: 0.082-0.085ms @ bs=1, 0.335-0.336ms @ bs=4, 0.498-0.498ms @ bs=6 (flat at all ctx ≥ 64K)
FA2 scales O(B) × O(L) per step: at bs=6/256K = 46.1ms vs TLI 0.5ms → 93× gap
speedup scales sub-linearly in L (≈O(L/K²) trend): 5×@32K → 70×@256K @bs=1; 32×@32K → 96×@128K @bs=4
Memory: TLI uses 1.4GB @ bs=6/256K vs FA2 27.6GB (20× memory advantage)
Total 24/24 arms clean across 8 GPUs. No errors, no co-resident contention.
verdict: E178 confirms the LoDA-SA sparse attention operator (K1=128 + tail32 + far-skip + K2=1024) delivers 5-93× decode-attention speedup over FlashAttention2 dense across batch sizes 1-6 and context lengths 32K-256K, with near-constant latency independent of context length. This is the strongest evidence yet for the DAC paper's performance claim.
